challenges.title: Two-Sum with Hash Map Lookups
challenges.problem_statement: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target. Each input has exactly one solution.
challenges.starter_code:
def two_sum(nums: list[int], target: int) -> list[int]:
    pass
challenges.unit_test_suite:
def test_two_sum():
    assert two_sum([2, 7, 11, 15], 9) == [0, 1]
    assert two_sum([3, 2, 4], 6) == [1, 2]
    assert two_sum([3, 3], 6) == [0, 1]
explanation_steps: 1. Initialize empty hash map seen.
2. Traverse array, compute complement.
3. Return indices if complement found; else store current index.

challenges.title: Hierarchical Organization Chart Depth via Recursive CTE
challenges.problem_statement: Given an employee table with emp_id and manager_id, write a recursive CTE to compute the hierarchical depth and management path of every employee.
challenges.starter_code: WITH RECURSIVE org_chart AS ( /* ... */ ) SELECT * FROM org_chart;
challenges.reference_solution:
WITH RECURSIVE org_chart AS (
    SELECT emp_id, manager_id, name, 0 AS depth, CAST(name AS TEXT) AS path
    FROM employees
    WHERE manager_id IS NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT e.emp_id, e.manager_id, e.name, oc.depth + 1, oc.path || ' -> ' || e.name
    FROM employees e
    JOIN org_chart oc ON e.manager_id = oc.emp_id
)
SELECT emp_id, name, depth, path FROM org_chart ORDER BY depth, emp_id;
explanation_steps: 1. Anchor query selects root nodes (manager_id IS NULL).
2. Recursive query joins child employees on parent emp_id.
3. Depth increments monotonically by 1 per level.

challenges.title: PSR-4 Lightweight Router with Middleware Pipeline
challenges.problem_statement: Implement an HTTP request router supporting strict typing, variable route parameters, and chained middleware pipes.
challenges.reference_solution:
<?php declare(strict_types=1);

class Router {
    /** @var array<string, array<string, callable>> */
    private array $routes = [];
    /** @var array<callable> */
    private array $middlewares = [];

    public function use(callable $mw): self {
        $this->middlewares[] = $mw;
        return $this;
    }

    public function add(string $method, string $path, callable $handler): self {
        $this->routes[strtoupper($method)][$path] = $handler;
        return $this;
    }

    public function dispatch(string $method, string $path, array $req = []): mixed {
        $method = strtoupper($method);
        if (!isset($this->routes[$method][$path])) {
            throw new RuntimeException('Route not found', 404);
        }
        $pipeline = array_reduce(
            array_reverse($this->middlewares),
            fn($next, $mw) => fn($r) => $mw($r, $next),
            fn($r) => ($this->routes[$method][$path])($r)
        );
        return $pipeline($req);
    }
}
challenges.unit_test_suite:
<?php
$r = new Router();
$r->use(function($req, $next) { $req['trace'] = ['mw1']; return $next($req); });
$r->add('GET', '/users', fn($req) => array_merge($req['trace'], ['handler']));
$res = $r->dispatch('GET', '/users');
assert($res === ['mw1', 'handler']);
explanation_steps: 1. Store routes by method and exact path.
2. Compose middleware stack using functional array_reduce.
3. Execute pipeline through final handler.

challenges.title: Thread-Safe Bounded Object Pool using ReentrantLock
challenges.problem_statement: Design a generic, thread-safe object pool with fixed capacity that blocks acquiring threads when empty and releases cleanly.
explanation_steps: 1. Guard internal queue with ReentrantLock.
2. Use Condition variable notEmpty to coordinate waiting threads.
3. Always release locks in finally blocks.

challenges.title: Bounded Worker Pool with Graceful Context Cancellation
challenges.problem_statement: Implement a worker pool in Go that manages N concurrent worker goroutines, accepts task closures, and terminates cleanly when context is canceled.
explanation_steps: 1. Launch fixed number of worker goroutines reading from tasks channel.
2. Select on both ctx.Done() and task channel to handle cancellation.
3. Wait on sync.WaitGroup during Stop() to guarantee clean worker teardown.
